contentBlocks.text: Last week you wrote a formal essay. This week: public speaking, a related but genuinely different skill!

A speech needs a structure listeners can follow by ear, since they can't reread a confusing sentence like they could in an essay: a strong opening hook to grab attention, 2-3 clear main points, and a memorable closing. Pick a topic you know well, and outline a short speech about it: one opening hook, two main points, one closing thought.
You just outlined a real speech structure! Tomorrow we'll learn delivery skills: eye contact, pacing, and voice.

objectives: Understand a speech's structure: hook, main points, closing
Outline a short speech with all three parts
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's formal-essay-writing work briefly.
2. Introduce speech structure, contrasting it with essay structure.
3. Have the child outline their own short speech.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's delivery-skills lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a familiar, simple topic (a favorite hobby or game) to outline rather than an abstract one
Ready for more: ask the child why a listener needs a clearer structure than a reader does
Opens this week's public-speaking thread, a genuinely different skill from last week's written-essay work
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended outlining activity — check that the speech includes a genuine hook, two distinct main points, and a real closing thought.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 8 Speaking and Listening standard SL.8.4: presenting claims and findings with clear organization, opening this week's public-speaking thread from the course's own description.

generationData.instructions: Outline a short speech: hook, two main points, closing.
